Keyboard Shortcuts

Complete keyboard shortcut reference for Windows, Linux, and Mac.

This page lists every keyboard shortcut registered in Hypertask for Windows/Linux and Mac.

The App shell surfaces shortcuts 1 through 6 apply only when the app-shell rail is enabled.

On Mac, switch boards with Ctrl + 0-9, not Cmd + 0-9. Mac browsers reserve Cmd + 1-9 for tab switching.

On Mac, Ctrl + K opens the command palette in addition to Cmd + K.

Mobile comment composer gesture actions

On mobile devices, the comment composer keeps dictation as the primary input method with simplified controls:

  • Dictate first, then refine with the Improve with AI option (opens a focused bottom sheet on mobile)
  • Send remains the secondary, accessible action
  • The Improve with AI trigger provides inline text enhancement without replacing dictation as the primary entry point

On mobile, start with dictation and tap Improve with AI to refine your comments without leaving the input flow.

Mobile in-app gestures

  • On mobile, press and hold a comment to open the Command Center with comment actions at the top. Edit comment is first when you wrote the comment.

Command Palette

Search commandsType to filterType to filter
Execute commandEnterEnter
Navigate through filtered commandsArrow keysArrow keys

The Command Palette lists board and section actions, including "Hide column", "Show columns", "Archive board", "Delete board", and more. Use Ctrl+K and type keywords like "hide", "show", "archive", "delete" to quickly access relevant actions.

Board settings from Ctrl+K

When you search for "Board settings" in the Command Palette using Ctrl+K or Cmd+K, the board picker now preselects the board you came from. This works whether you're on a ticket page, board page, or another view - even if you previously had a different team open in settings. Press Esc to cancel and restore your previous state.

Try it: open any ticket, press Ctrl+K, type "board", pick "Board settings". The board picker shows that ticket's board and preselects the right team.

Hiding and Showing Columns

To hide a column using the Command Palette:

  1. Open the Command Palette: Ctrl + K
  2. Type "hide" to find the "Hide column" action
  3. Press Enter to hide the active (hovered/last-clicked) column directly
  4. The Command Palette closes automatically after execution

To show previously hidden columns:

  1. Open the Command Palette: Ctrl + K
  2. Type "show" to find the "Show columns" action
  3. Press Enter to reveal all hidden sections

"Hide column" now targets the last clicked or currently hovered section rather than cycling through sections, making it easier to hide the specific column you're working with. The "Empty columns" command also reads the current state and filters both the Kanban view groups and the table view groups, showing "Show empty columns" when they're hidden and "Hide empty columns" when they're visible.

An empty view keeps its visible columns on screen, even when empty columns are hidden. Your saved setting does not change. Add a ticket and the other empty columns hide again. Columns you hid individually stay hidden.

Board palette

Press Ctrl + B (Windows/Linux) or Cmd + B (Mac) to show the board palette overlay. On the left rail, the board palette displays your user account row with:

  • Email or handle - Click to open the account switcher dialog
  • Avatar - Click to open Account & Profile settings

This provides quick access to switching workspaces or reviewing your account configuration without leaving the current board.

The board palette joins Ctrl+K as a non-intrusive way to access workspace settings while staying in context.

Open Latest Updates

Press Ctrl + K (Windows/Linux) or Cmd + K (Mac) then search for "Latest Updates" in the board palette or command palette to open the Latest Updates panel from any route in the app. This provides quick access to see recent activity across your boards without leaving your current view.

Global Alt+Number board shortcuts

Before: On the table view or any board view, Alt + 1-7 shortcuts did nothing even when the app-shell rail was supposed to be active, causing them to behave as no-ops.

After: When the rail is enabled, Alt + 2-7 now correctly switch to their corresponding surfaces (Board = 2, Table = 3, Calendar = 4, AI Chat dock = 5, and Search = 6) from any view. On Mac, the global board switcher uses Ctrl + 2-7 instead of Cmd to avoid interfering with tab switching.

The app-shell rail and global Alt+Number shortcuts were designed to provide tactile, one-hand navigation across main surfaces. Enabling the rail (via account menu or command palette) unlocks these skips so they work reliably everywhere, not only on the rail itself.

Time reports quick-log

Quick-log time directly from the board or a task card using Ctrl + K:

  • On a board or task card - Press Ctrl + K to open the quick-log dialog preconfigured for the selected card.
  • On an open ticket - Press Ctrl + K to instantly jump to the per-ticket time log modal, skipping the intermediate step of selecting the ticket from the board list.

The quick-log interface supports Hours and Minutes fields, board and user filters per entry, and works across time zones with per-entry local-noon timestamps for accurate log association with the logged day.

Timer shortcuts

Time tracking shortcuts are available when time tracking is enabled for your board or task:

  • App shell rail - Press 7 on the rail to open the running-timers view
  • Task detail - Press Option + T or Alt+T to start or stop the open task timer

The timer indicator appears in the task card and task detail, showing whether a timer is running for that task.

See the Time Tracking page for full details.

System-theme prediction

When you open the Command Palette with Ctrl+K (or Cmd+K on Mac), theme-related options now display context-appropriate labels to make system-theme mode predictable. Retired numeric theme modes (1-5) redirect safely to the Appearance settings with your in-session command state preserved.

Theme options in the command palette now adapt to your system theme and gracefully redirect legacy theme choices to Appearance settings.

Copy current page URL

When you open the Command Palette with Ctrl+K or Cmd+K, the action "Copy current page URL" copies the complete browser address, including the board, view, task, filters, and section. The action is available everywhere Ctrl+K opens, including task detail, calendar, and inbox views.

The action is available to everyone.

Use everywhere, including Settings

Ctrl + K (Windows/Linux) or Cmd + K (Mac) now opens the Command Palette on every signed-in page. This includes:

  • Boards, tickets, inbox, and search (existing behavior)
  • My Tasks view
  • All settings pages, such as Settings & General, Board general, and Appearance

On Mac, Ctrl + K also works in addition to Cmd + K.

Public/sign-in pages, including the sign-in page, still ignore this shortcut.

Escape behavior in Settings:

  • First Esc closes the command menu and keeps you in Settings
  • A second Esc exits Settings as usual

This makes the command palette consistently available for board actions, views, and shortcuts throughout the app.

Mobile in-app gestures

  • On mobile, press and hold a comment to open the Command Center with comment actions at the top. Edit comment is first when you wrote the comment.
  • Dictation remains the primary input method on mobile; Tap Improve with AI to refine your comments without leaving the input flow

Mobile page exit gesture

On mobile, pressing Esc in the full-screen Pages view now exits via the back action - just like other views in the app. With text typed but unsaved, Esc clears the unsaved draft. Without text, a single Esc closes the page and stays on the task.

Ctrl+J board chip

When you press Ctrl+J, the new task box shows which board the task will land on, using the same board chip UI as the AI chat box. The chip appears as soon as the box opens, on every page: a board, a ticket, the inbox and views that mix boards. On a board or ticket page it shows that page's board.

Board selection logic:

  • Focused ticket's board: If a ticket is visible and focused in the inbox, Ctrl+J places the new task on that ticket's board.
  • Open board split: If there's no focused ticket, the task goes on the open board split.
  • All or Important: If no board is in context, Ctrl+J uses All or Important as a default board.

Click the chip before saving to change the board.

From the inbox, Ctrl+J is the fastest way to start a new task on a specific board without exiting the feed.

Sending from the Ctrl+J new task box

The new task box sends with the same shortcut as comments and descriptions, so Enter is free for paragraphs.

ActionWindows/LinuxMac
Send the new taskCtrl + EnterCmd + Enter
Start a new paragraphEnterEnter

The hint under the box names the shortcut. One press creates one task with everything you typed, and your note stays in the box if the task fails.

New Task board shortcut hint

Hover over the board chip in New Task to see its keyboard shortcut: Ctrl + Shift + B on Windows and Linux, or Cmd + Shift + B on Mac. The same shortcut appears below the task box. Click the chip or use that shortcut to choose a board. Press Esc to cancel without losing your draft.
